correctness.rationale: The resolving-arm lemma was checked for vertex and edge codes; an admissible set meets at least t-1 arms. The vertex-domination minimum follows exact 3-interval coverage with the depth-one center constraint. The edge-domination minimum follows exhaustive center-selected, center-absent-no-depth-one and center-absent-with-depth-one cases, with exact 4-edge intervals and an arm-support correction for length-two arms. Algebra of ceiling functions gives the sharp iff. A distinct graph-distance brute force verified the arm-resolution lemma on 2,688 subsets and the minima in 51 small instances, including mixed boundary arms, and modular identity checks covered 42,294 additional profiles. Computation confirms cases but the infinite proof is the interval argument. Main risks: unnoticed error in case exhaustiveness or the arm-resolving equivalence; explicitly stress-tested with direct code.

value.rationale: The 2022 source explicitly asks to characterize equality trees; this establishes the complete iff for the natural family of all spiders whose edges have been subdivided at least once, with arbitrary numbers and unequal lengths of arms. Exact mod-3 and mod-4 formulas explain the coverage-radius competition, and the five-edge spider family gives unbounded strict gap t-1. The result is not an arbitrary finite instance, routine restatement of a bound, or an isolated parameter computation; it supplies a structural boundary answering a motivated open-problem subcase.
